about: The epistle of the Fourth Sunday of Advent. Paul takes the verdict away from the Corinthians and from himself alike — it belongs to the Lord, and it is not given until He comes.

seg.tr: Brethren: Let people regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
What is required of stewards is that each be found faithful.
It matters very little to me whether I am judged by you or by a human court; I do not even judge myself.

fn.w025: An adjective used as a noun: “a very small thing”. It is the superlative of parvus.
fn.w033: Day in the sense of a court sitting, as in the day of the Lord. The Greek behind it says a human day, that is, a human tribunal.

seg.tr: For I am not conscious of anything against myself, yet this does not justify me; the Lord is the One who judges me.
Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light the things hidden in darkness and reveal the counsels of hearts; then each will receive praise from God.

fn.w067: A plural participle used as a noun: the hidden things.
